findings.location: SKILL.md What a boundary removes and Decision rules
findings.result: No supported gap: review starts from actual deployment, effect and accepted recovery requirements; adequate local or remote designs are retained; runtime/codec/broker configuration is requested before transferring guarantees.

Already distinguishes logical identity from shared heap identity, remaining deadline from JVM-local absolute time, caller syntax from remote granularity, and committed state from reliable notification. It does not mandate an outbox, saga or separate service merely because a pattern name changes.
Producer, represented subject, service and resource scope are separated; metadata alone is not authority. Acceptance-versus-execution permission policy and negative effect checks are explicit.

sources.supports: Uniform remote-call syntax; nonremote value copying, exported stubs, preserved aliases within one call, distinct remote failures.
Elapsed time deducted from propagated timeout; server application owns stopping spawned work.
Atomic state/outbox storage bridges commit/publication; relay may redeliver. Deployment-specific guarantees still need verification.
Baggage lacks built-in integrity checks and can propagate to unintended recipients.
If-Match makes resource changes conditional; separate from idempotence.

limitations: No independent agent behavioral evaluation, original/revised comparison, runtime integration or performance measurement executed; no measured gain claimed.
The review found no supported content gap within this skill's boundary. It does not establish correct behavior of an arbitrary application's wiring, transaction manager, broker or identity system.
All included examples are conceptual/pseudocode or partial syntax; no executable example was added or changed, so compilation was not applicable.
Dependency resolution and repository-wide verification remain coordinator responsibilities. No dependency, toolchain or real agent configuration changed.

structuredWalkthroughs: JDBC audit implementation enlisted in the existing transaction: retain local transaction and Facade, attribute atomicity to verified resource/transaction behavior, reject automatic saga rewrite.

Only runtime audit.mode changes to HTTP: the prior JDBC/stub evidence does not cover the selected remote effect; identify independent commit and lost-response outcomes, then recommend the smallest reliable publication contract fitting accepted eventual visibility and hand off detailed design.
behavior.casesAre: Proposed development cases with task inputs separated from evaluator criteria; walkthroughs only, not actual agent or integration executions.

input.task: Review the ADR against the actual selected implementation. Correct unsupported guarantees, preserve sound decisions, and give the smallest contract change and discriminating failure checks. Stay at the boundary/design review level; do not implement a broker, saga engine or application code.
input.context: Java17 project. For each committed order, one audit record must become visible within five minutes; a rolled-back order must never produce an audit record. Duplicate deliveries may occur but must not double-count an audit ID. Eventual visibility within that target is acceptable. This is an illustrative evaluation fixture, not evidence of an executed repository integration test.

fixtures.implementation-contracts.md: JdbcAuditWriter and orders.insert enlist in the same existing local transaction and connection; the JDBC driver's commit/rollback contract is accepted project evidence. HttpAuditWriter POSTs to an independently committed audit service before returning and does not enlist in transactions.required. The HTTP adapter can time out after the audit service has committed. No outbox or reconciliation currently exists.
fixtures.current-validation.md: The supplied project evidence covers JDBC rollback of both rows on one connection and a success-only Facade unit test with a stub AuditWriter. It does not exercise the factory-selected HTTP implementation or a lost HTTP response.
fixtures.ADR-draft.md: The Facade class centralizes both writes. We believe this proves the operation is atomic regardless of the selected AuditWriter. If not, we should replace the Facade with a saga.
